_This page is generated from src/exit-codes.ts, so it says what the tool does._

`run` and `score` exit with one of these codes. `summary.json` in the output directory holds the same number as `exit`, and `evaluate` returns it as `exit`. [Use it in CI](../guides/ci.md) shows how to gate on them.

| Code  | Name        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`   | ok          | Every run is valid and every pass bar is reached.                                                                                                                                 |
| `1`   | bar         | A pass bar was not reached: `--min-score`, or a case's `minScore`.                                                                                                                |
| `2`   | usage       | A wrong command line, case file, config file or subject, or an unsupported platform. One line on standard error, before any run. `validate` also exits 2 when it finds a problem. |
| `3`   | invalid     | More of the planned runs are invalid than `--max-invalid` allows (default: any), or a subject directory changed while the command ran. The message says which.                    |
| `4`   | partial     | `--max-cost` or `--max-duration` stopped the command. Runs that never ran are not invalid. Continue with `--resume`.                                                              |
| `5`   | error       | An internal failure that is not a usage error. The stack trace is on standard error, and `results.json` says `partial` is `error`.                                                |
| `130` | interrupted | SIGINT or SIGTERM ended the command. The results so far are written first.                                                                                                        |

## When several apply

The first of these wins: `2` (usage), `130` (interrupted), `5` (error), `4` (partial), `3` (invalid), `1` (bar). A command that stopped at `--max-cost` and also has an invalid run exits 4, and one that has an invalid run and a missed bar exits 3. A usage error is raised before any run, so nothing else can apply with it.

## An invalid-run budget

By default one invalid run is enough to exit 3. `--max-invalid <fraction>` allows some. The command exits 3 only when the invalid runs divided by the planned runs of the cases that apply is greater than the fraction. A run that did not run, because a limit stopped the command, is not invalid and is not counted.

```sh
# 3 runs are planned, 1 is invalid: 1/3 is not greater than 0.5, so the command exits 0 (or 1 if a bar is missed).
skill-evals score --subject ./skills --reps 3 --max-invalid 0.5
```

The value is a number from 0 to 1. `maxInvalid` in the config file sets the default.

## Other commands

| Command    | Codes                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `check`    | `0` when every installed harness answered; `1` when one failed its run; `3` when the subject directory changed while it ran; `2` for a wrong command line. A harness that is not installed is a row of the table, not a failure. |
| `validate` | `0` when the suite has no problem (warnings do not count); `2` when it has at least one.                                                                                                                                         |
| `list`     | `0`, or `2` for a wrong command line or case file.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `plan`     | `0`, or `2` for a wrong command line, case file or output directory. `--dry-run` on `run` and `score` prints the same and exits `0`.                                                                                             |

An internal failure in any command exits `5` with a stack trace on standard error.
